::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Maximum, over all unit vectors, of directional derivative CALCULUS 3](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/3472846/maximum-over-all-unit-vectors-of-directional-derivative-calculus-3), asked by [hexaquark](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/704928/hexaquark) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2019-12-11; [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)):

> Given $f(x,y,z) = x^2 +3xz + \dfrac{y^3}{3}$ I'm asked to find the maximum value, ***over all unit vectors,*** of $D_{u} f(1,2,-1)$.   
>
> Attempt :  
> $$\nabla f = \langle f_x , f_y, f_z \rangle = \langle 2x + 3z, y^2 , 3x \rangle$$
> $$D_u f = || \nabla f(1,2,-1)|| = || (-1,4,-3)|| = \sqrt{26}$$
>
> I feel like i'm  missing a step somewhere, particularly something concerning the " all unit vectors". 
> Thank you for help.
:::

Recall that $D_u f(P) = \nabla f(P) \cdot u$, so
$$D_u f(P) = \Vert \nabla f(P) \Vert \, \Vert u \Vert \,\cos\theta$$
where $\theta$ is the angle between $\nabla f(P)$ and $u$.  Remember $\Vert u \Vert =1$ and $|\cos\theta|\leq 1$.  So the maximum value of $D_u f(P)$, over all unit vectors $u$, occurs when $u$ points in the same direction as $\nabla f(P)$ (i.e., $\cos\theta =1 \implies \theta = 0$).  In this case, $D_u(P) = \Vert \nabla f(P) \Vert$.
